answer: One defence is Erasure-coded chunk custody proof: chunks that only a real custodian can return, and the hollow of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. A clone farm can generate keys forever, but it cannot generate chunks that only a real custodian can return a hundred times without paying a hundred times over, and the atlas of that asymmetry is what keeps the network honest. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the jetty of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
